title: Functional Biomechanical Analysis in Patients Who Underwent Lateral Ankle Ligament Repair With Augmentation
official: Functional Biomechanical Analysis in Patients Who Underwent Lateral Ankle Ligament Repair With Augmentation
summary:
Chronic lateral ankle instability is a common condition in athletic populations and may lead to persistent biomechanical alterations despite appropriate management. This condition typically develops following one or more ankle sprains and is characterized by a sensation of instability, episodes of the ankle giving way, pain, or discomfort during physical or sporting activities. When conventional treatments such as rehabilitation, physiotherapy, and activity modification do not provide sufficient improvement, surgical ligament repair may be recommended.

Although this surgery generally restores ankle stability, there is currently limited evidence regarding how lower-limb function evolves following the procedure. In particular, there is no established objective reference measure to assess functional recovery and support healthcare professionals in making decisions regarding rehabilitation or return to sport.

The prospective interventional comparative analysis proposed in this study aims to evaluate surgery-induced changes in ankle and lower-limb movement and function that can be objectively quantified through biomechanical motion analysis.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Standard indications for lateral ankle ligament repair surgery for chronic lateral ankle instability refractory to conservative treatment.
* Participation in physical activity and/or sports at least once weekly before the onset of symptoms leading to the surgical indication.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Concomitant surgical procedures likely to alter postoperative recovery.
* History of major lower-limb fractures.
* Associated injuries involving the lower limbs or lumbar spine.
* Any other surgery performed within 6 months prior to the index procedure.
